title: Universal Printer Generation Priorities and Reproductive Capability Graph
correction: Generation-1 is itself the first universal technology printer. RGB/light emission, energy storage, conductance, passive electronics, sensing, actuation, environment control and an active switching/logic route are G1 acceptance functions, although performance and local-material provenance may initially be below mature commercial equivalents.

process_grammar.meaning: reduce selected functional phase concentration by adding compatible carrier/base while maintaining declared total-flow/geometry constraint
spatially vary feed/material composition over path/layer/volume
introduce liquid/gas/reactive phase into porous or printed region
remove volatile carrier/solvent or trapped gas under bounded thermal/pressure conditions
densify/transform material with localized or global energy treatment
add thin conductive/functional film by qualified electrodeposition/vapor/fine-deposition route
mill/ablate/etch only through a material/process-specific qualified removal module
add scarce functional species to abundant carrier at controlled low fraction; requires material-specific evidence
apply controlled strain during cure/cooling when validated
apply electric/magnetic conditioning when material requires it
meter gas/liquid/electrolyte into cavity or porous region
reduce cavity/chamber pressure to process target
close pressure/fluid/electrical boundary after preclosure verification
remove/rework failed region within bounded service geometry

priority_sequence.objective: Printer-1 fabricates and commissions a smaller, higher-finesse universal printer of the same functional class.
outputs: active-switch/logic route or seed-die integration until printed switch route qualifies
priority_sequence.rationale: Printer-μ becomes both a self-reproduction proof and a precision manufacturing instrument for upgrading its parent.

priority_sequence.objective: Printer-μ and Printer-1 cooperatively fabricate higher-finesse toolheads, sensors, manifolds, electronics, bearings/interfaces and calibration artifacts to upgrade Printer-1 and then build Printer-2 at the original scale.
priority_sequence.outcome: two same-scale compatible printers plus one micro/finesse printer, with increased printable fraction, lower seed dependence and improved precision.

priority_sequence.objective: The printer family fabricates the first tethered/free-range mobile UTP agents able to cooperate on structures exceeding any chamber.
outputs: one or more dexterous print/manipulation arms
local feed intake and material passport station
power/data tether or local power module
shared coordinate frame and multi-agent scheduler
priority_sequence.outcome: scalable on-site construction/manufacturing in terrestrial, lunar, orbital or asteroid environments.

reproduction_metrics.mass_fraction: fraction of child-machine mass fabricated by parent family
reproduction_metrics.part_fraction: fraction of child unique parts fabricated
reproduction_metrics.function_fraction: fraction of required functional basis reproducible
reproduction_metrics.critical_dependency_fraction: fraction of single-point critical items still imported
reproduction_metrics.energy_fraction: fraction of child manufacturing energy sourced locally
reproduction_metrics.material_fraction: fraction of child material mass locally sourced/recycled
reproduction_metrics.calibration_independence: fraction of metrology/calibration chain reproducible without external lab
reproduction_metrics.note: A printer can be fully functioning while still seed-dependent. Self-reproduction completeness is measured continuously rather than as a binary claim.
